topic: A fieldwork plan that can be repeated
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: A fieldwork plan that can be repeated
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立盲听答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
transcript:
Maya: Our pond survey is scheduled for Saturday. Should everyone choose whichever sampling point looks most interesting?
Tutor: No. That would make a second visit hard to compare with the first. Use the eight numbered points on the map.
Maya: The original plan had ten points, but two are behind a locked gate. I have marked those as inaccessible rather than pretending they do not exist.
Tutor: Good. Record that exclusion. What will you measure?
Maya: Water temperature and the number of visible insects during a three-minute observation. We are not claiming to count every animal in the pond.
Tutor: What about equipment?
Maya: Teams will use the same thermometer model. We will check the readings together before separating, so a faulty instrument is easier to notice.
Tutor: Rain is forecast in the afternoon. Will the visit be cancelled?
Maya: Only if the bank is unsafe. Otherwise we will note the rainfall and begin at ten, as planned. Weather becomes part of the record, not something we silently remove.
Tutor: And photographs?
Maya: One photograph of each marked point, facing north. No identifiable visitors. Files will be named with the point number and date.
Tutor: Finally, who keeps the raw notes?
Maya: The department archive. We will submit a summary, but the original sheets will remain available for checking.

transfer.writing: Write an evidence-based paragraph of 120–160 words about planning repeatable fieldwork. State one claim, support it with a relevant example, acknowledge a limitation, and explain what further evidence would change your conclusion. Use a new example; do not copy the passage.
